Pranama. In this profound darkness, please know that you are deeply seen, cherished, and held by divine grace. In the very first chapter of the Gita, the valiant Arjuna fell weeping into his chariot seat, his spirit consumed by heavy despondency (*Vishada*). What has drained the vitality and meaning from your days? Why does the inner voice whisper that things will never improve? A heavy blanket of numbness and emptiness Loss of interest in everything that used to bring joy Feeling like a burden to everyone around me Struggling to find any reason or energy to get through the day A quiet despair that no one truly understands

You named “it has been like this for a while”. Depression is not weakness of character; it is your soul's chariot collapsing under accumulated, unexpressed grief and exhaustion (*Arjuna Vishada*). Tamasika Vishada (तामसिक विषाद / Soul Despondency) When *Tamas* (inertia, fog, obscurity) overpowers the intellect, it veils the soul's natural effulgence (*Sat-Chit-Ananda*) and paints reality as an eternal grey dungeon. Bhagavad Gita 2.3 & 6.5 Yield not to unmanliness, O Partha! It does not befit you. Cast off this petty faint-heartedness and arise, O conqueror of foes!

Elevate yourself through the power of your mind; do not degrade yourself. For the mind alone is your greatest ally, and the mind alone can be your greatest enemy. Krishna does not condemn Arjuna for collapsing; he stands over him with fierce, unconditional love and reminds him of the lion sleeping within. You are not the darkness; you are the awareness observing the darkness. CBT Behavioral Activation & The Micro-Flame Step 1 (The Micro-Action Rule): When despair says 'do nothing', refuse to negotiate for a massive achievement. Choose one microscopic victory: drinking one glass of water, making the bed, or opening a window to let in sunlight. Step 2 (Cognitive Externalization): Label the voice of hopelessness: 'That is the depression talking, not my true soul. It is a passing biological cloud, not the sky.' Step 3 (Somatic Sunlight): Step into the natural light for 10 minutes. Feel the warmth on your face as the cosmic blessing of Surya. Step 4 (Safety Harbor): If the pain is unbearable, reach out immediately to a trusted companion or our Safe Harbor helplines. Asking for help is an act of supreme courage.

Pranama. To give your honest labor and receive hostility, malice, or unjust criticism in return is a bitter test of character. What toxic interaction or unreasonable manager/peer has disturbed your peace? Why do you allow their poisoned opinion to dictate your inner sense of competence and dignity? A toxic boss who takes credit for my work and belittles me Spiteful office gossip and petty politics Harsh, public criticism that felt humiliating Being passed over for a well-deserved promotion Dreading Monday morning and every interaction at work

You named “it has been like this for a while”. You have permitted the confusion or malice of another person to disturb your inner temple. Their criticism says everything about their own inner disorder, and very little about you. Titiksha & Lokasangraha (तितिक्षा & लोकसङ्ग्रह) *Titiksha* is noble forbearance—the ability to endure worldly unpleasantness without losing your center. You do not let their mud soil your white lotus. Bhagavad Gita 12.15 He by whom the world is not agitated and who cannot be agitated by the world, who is freed from excessive joy, envy, fear, and anxiety—he is dearly cherished by Me. To be unshakeable amidst worldly turbulence is the pinnacle of spiritual strength. Maintain professional excellence, document your work diligently, but keep your emotional sovereignty locked safely within. CBT Professional Detachment & The Glass Shield Step 1 (The Glass Shield Visualization): Picture an invisible shield of diamond between you and their harsh words. The words bounce off the glass; they cannot enter your soul. Step 2 (Separate Data from Venom): Strip away the emotional insults. Is there a grain of useful work data? If yes, keep the data; discard the venom. Step 3 (Document & Protect): Keep clear records of facts and deliverables without emotional language. Step 4 (Affirmation): 'Their behavior is their karma; my poise and self-respect are mine.'

Pranama. The arena of trial stands before you, and fear casts a long shadow across your courage. Remember, even the greatest archer Arjuna trembled and dropped his bow on the threshold of Kurukshetra. What test, interview, or evaluation is causing this terror of falling short? Why do you equate the score or verdict of this test with your fundamental worth as a human being? Upcoming exams or critical career interviews Fear of disappointing my parents or family Comparison with peers who seem ahead Dread that a single failure will ruin my future Paralysis that prevents me from even studying

You named “it has been like this for a while”. You have attached your identity, dignity, and future happiness to a singular temporal milestone, mistaking an event for your soul's entire destiny. Adhyasa (अध्यास / Superimposition of Worth) & Phala-Bhiti Superimposing your immortal, radiant worth onto an external scorecard creates existential terror. An exam tests only prepared data, never the boundless divine spark within you. Bhagavad Gita 2.38 & 2.48 Perform your prescribed duty poise-established in Yoga, abandoning attachment, O Dhananjaya. Remain completely equanimous in success and failure; for equanimity alone is called Yoga. True mastery (*Yoga*) is unwavering composure regardless of victory or defeat. When you surrender the desperate obsession with winning, the energy wasted on panic returns to fuel your focus. CBT Cognitive Reframing: Event vs. Identity Step 1 (Cognitive Disentanglement): Write: 'Failure is an event in time, not a character flaw. A test evaluates current preparation, not my intrinsic worth.' Step 2 (The 5-Year Horizon): Ask: 'Five years from today, will this one exam define my capacity to love, create, and be kind?' It will be a small pebble in the river of your journey. Step 3 (Chunking the Duty): Break your preparation into a tiny, non-intimidating 25-minute block. Commit only to this single block with full heart, dedicating the effort to learning rather than outcome. Step 4 (Affirmation): Recite: 'I am the conscious warrior, not the scorecard.'

Pranama. Envy is a silent poison that steals our joy while keeping our eyes glued to another's garden. It is natural to feel this pang when surrounded by relentless displays of others' triumphs. Whose success, lifestyle, or milestone is triggering this sting of comparison? Why do you believe their abundance implies a deficiency in your own destiny? Seeing peers get promoted, married, or praised Social media feeds making my daily life look pathetic Bitterness that others had advantages I was denied Feeling that life is an unfair zero-sum contest Ashamed of feeling secret delight when someone slips

You named “it has been like this for a while”. You are looking at another's highlight reel and forgetting that every soul has its own unique debts (*Prarabdha Karma*) and trials that remain unseen beneath the surface. Matsarya (मात्सर्य / Envy) & Asuya (Fault-finding) Matsarya is an illusion of scarcity. It assumes that there is only one crown in the universe, and if someone else wears it, you are left empty. In truth, the cosmos is infinite. Bhagavad Gita 4.22 & 12.13 Content with whatever comes unasked, free from the dualities of life, devoid of all envy, and poised equally in success and failure—such a person, though acting, is never bound. Krishna describes the enlightened being as *Vimatsara*—utterly free from envy. When you delight in another's joy (*Mudita*), you instantly double your own happiness without paying any price. CBT Mudita Cultivation & The Scarcity Antidote Step 1 (Bless the Trigger): When envy strikes, mentally whisper: 'May they be safe, happy, and continue to prosper.' This breaks the neurochemical loop of hostility. Step 2 (The Unseen Ledger): Remind yourself: 'I see their stage performance, not their private tears, hospital visits, or inner demons.' Everyone carries a cross. Step 3 (Digital Fast): Turn off social media notifications for 48 hours. Redirect your gaze to your own sacred garden. Step 4 (Audit Your Blessings): List 3 specific advantages, talents, or freedoms you enjoy that someone in the world is desperately praying for.
